title: The honored guest
hookLine: Dhanna's rock; a shelf of five things for God
carry: the murti is an honored guest
last: THE MALA: ONE FULL ROUND OF 108.

lines: IT COMES DOWN TO FIVE THINGS.
cards: In many Hindu homes there's a small shrine. In a big house it might be a whole room; in a student apartment, a shelf above the desk.
In a lot of kitchens it's a little alcove near the stove, with a picture of Krishna leaning against the spice jars and a lamp lit every morning for as long as anyone remembers.
It's called the mandir, the temple, or the puja room, even when it's only a shelf. And a simple one can come down to five things.

teach.b: Who lives on that shelf? Dhanna was a farm boy in Rajasthan, and the story told of him goes like this. He watched a brahmin worship a sacred stone every morning, and begged for one of his own.
To get rid of him, the brahmin handed him an ordinary rock.

teach.h: HE WOULDN'T EAT UNTIL GOD DID.
teach.b: Dhanna took it home, set it in a clean place, and at mealtime put his own food in front of it and waited for God to eat. God didn't. So Dhanna didn't either.
Days went by, the boy hungry, stubborn and sure. And in the story, God came and ate from his plate. A plain rock, offered to with that much love, had become a home for God.
Many Hindus understand a murti, the image on the shrine, as a place where the divine is truly present, and welcome it as an honored guest; others see it as a focus for the mind; both are held.
That's why the five simple things are what a good host offers.
One, the image itself, the guest. Two, a lamp, for light. Three, a flower, something beautiful, given away.
Four, a bell, rung to begin, to call the attention of the divine, many say, and your own. Five, water, the first thing you'd offer anyone who walks in. Nothing costly; Dhanna's rock cost nothing.
Keep it clean and a little apart, and remember: a shelf you pass every morning beats a perfect room you never enter.

teach.h: THE MURTI IS AN HONORED GUEST.
teach.b: The murti is an honored guest.

how: Many Hindu homes keep a small shrine, from a whole puja room to a kitchen shelf, with an image or picture of the family's deities, a lamp, flowers, a bell and water, where daily puja is offered.

o: five sacred items a priest carries to a temple
image, lamp, flower, bell and water on a home shrine
the five daily duties every Hindu must perform

games.q: what's on the shelf — tap the pairs.
p: the farm boy whose rock God ate from
calls the divine's attention, and yours
the first thing offered to a guest

s: in the story, Dhanna was given a priceless sacred stone
he was given an ordinary rock. his love made it a home for God.
nothing on the simple shelf needs to be expensive
a tea light, a leaf, a cup of water will do. the care counts, not the cost.
all Hindus understand the image the same way
many see it as a place where the divine is present; others as a focus for the mind. both are held.

games.q: you want to make a home shrine, but you live in a tiny apartment with no spare room. what do you do?
o: wait until you have a bigger place.
clear one shelf you pass every morning.
put it somewhere hidden, like under the stairs.
games.why: a clean shelf you pass every morning is better than a perfect room you never enter. many traditions avoid spots like under the stairs.

practice: Choose a place, a shelf, the corner of a dresser, a windowsill, and clear it.

Gather what you have: an image or a picture that means something to you, a candle or tea light, a flower or a leaf from outside, anything that rings, even a spoon on a glass, and a small cup of water, and set them down slowly.
If you can't do it right now, picture exactly where it will go, then sit in front of it and breathe.

wordCard.voice: Five objects. An image, a lamp, a flower, a bell, and water: what a good host sets out for the guest on a home shrine.

orig.note: Sanskrit: form, embodiment; the image at the center of a shrine.

carryVoice: Take this with you: the murti is an honored guest. Dhanna's rock was enough, and a shelf is plenty. One hundred eleven days in.
